title: Jaipur blue pottery
summary: Jaipur blue pottery is made from ground quartz, powdered glass and gum instead of clay, painted with cobalt blue and turquoise and fired at a low heat. Here you raise a slender vase on the wheel, then paint its bands with leaves, flowers and birds.
howToPlay: Look at the small vase in the frame: that is the shape to make.
Drag across the spinning clay, row by row, to set how wide each part of the vase is; the lit outline shows the target.
Pick cobalt, turquoise or quartz white from the swatches and tap a band to paint it like the target.
Press Check to see your stars.
rules: The vase has twelve rows; each row can be set from narrow to wide.
Shape counts for most of the score, glaze for the rest.
Each band must carry the glaze shown on the target; the painted motif (leaf, flower, bird, vine) follows the band.
Undo takes back your last change; Reshape returns to the clay.
Three stars for a close shape with every band in the right glaze.
heritageNote: Jaipur in Rajasthan is known for blue pottery: the body is a paste of ground quartz, powdered glass and gum rather than clay, painted with cobalt and copper oxides and fired at a low heat. Craftspeople trace the blue-and-turquoise flowers, birds and vines to Persian and Central Asian tile makers, and revived the craft in the twentieth century.
